text: Deadlines are a part of professional life, and handling them well is a valuable skill. The first step is good time management. Instead of seeing a deadline as a distant event, break the work into smaller daily tasks. This makes the project feel less overwhelming. Another important factor is prioritization. Not all tasks are equal, so focus on the most critical parts of the project first. Also, practice scope management. It is easy to keep adding new ideas, but this can delay your progress. Stick to the original plan and avoid unnecessary changes. Finally, never underestimate the power of communication. If you see a problem coming, tell your team or client early. They will often appreciate your honesty and may help you find a solution.
